chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'or two others from among others than you'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man is in a land of strangers, not finding a Muslim in it, the testimony of one who is not a Muslim would be allowed upon the bequest.'
ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of a non-Muslim accepted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Quran 5:106, establishing that in lands of diaspora (ghurba) devoid of Muslim witnesses, the testimony of non-Muslims is legally valid for witnessing a bequest. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of necessity (darura) and the flexibility of evidentiary rules to preserve religious rights when the ideal conditions of Muslim witnesshood are unattainable.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:106] or two others from among others than you. Heasws said: ‘If the man was in a land of strangers, not finding a Muslim in it, the testimony of one who is not a Muslim would be allowed upon the bequest’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has narrated the following: “About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ’. . .or two from people other than your people,’ [5:106] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘This applies when a man is away from his land where Muslims are not found, then appointing non-Muslims as witness to a will is permissible.’”
